observation_summary: The TimeSeries.createCopy(RegularTimePeriod, RegularTimePeriod) method throws an IllegalArgumentException when the calculated start and end indices for the requested time range are invalid (e.g., start > end), even when the requested range is simply empty. The user expects an empty series to be returned instead of an exception.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by an overly restrictive validation check. The code currently throws an exception if 'end < start' (lines 882-883). The fix requires modifying this validation logic to handle cases where the range is empty (e.g., by returning an empty series instead of throwing an exception), which is a classic 'Checking' defect type.
evidence_used: The problem is in that the int start and end indexes corresponding to given timePeriod are computed incorectly. Here I would expect an empty serie to be returned, not an exception.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the calculation of indices is involved, the primary failure is the validation logic (the check) that triggers an exception instead of handling the empty range gracefully.
